subject: Rate anchoring + consumption-tier swap for Concordia Labs renewal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal — rate anchoring + tiered consumption swap

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for the productive renewal discussion last week. I put together a concrete path that addresses Concordia's desire for predictable unit economics while keeping operational flexibility for the coming year. High level:

- 6-month anchored rate: keep current effective per-token rate for the first 6 months of the renewal to protect against short-term price variance.
- Tiered consumption swap thereafter: move to a blended tier schedule (3 tiers) tied to monthly consumption with soft thresholds and automatic true-up.
- Bridge credits: provide $75k in service credits up front to offset migration/implementation work and the first month's overage risk.
- Dedicated burst pool: guaranteed access to 8-card Dedicated burst capacity for scheduled runs (4x/day windows), with a defined cancel/backoff policy.

I've attached a draft SOW that folds these items into the renewal and a pricing model workbook with example math. If this looks directionally right, suggest a short call Tuesday to lock the numbers and get legal looped in.

Attachments: Concordia_SOW_v2.pdf, concordia_pricing_model_v3.xlsx

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Alicia — Ben here, stepping in to outline some practical guardrails that make the procurement ask workable without undermining the anchor:

- Minimum commit: we can accept a 40%-run-rate minimum commit, but we propose a 90-day ramp window where the anchor applies prorated — if consumption is below target after 90 days, the anchor rate is adjusted back on a prorated basis. This gives Concordia predictability while protecting Redwood from an extended under-commit.

- Burst pool pricing: no separate fixed fee for the burst reservation. Instead:
  * Scheduled windows: 4 x 2-hour blocks per day reserved (customer-defined schedules).
  * In-window usage charged at anchor rate (i.e., no premium inside the blocks).
  * Out-of-window access permitted at 1.4x anchor rate; Redwood will offer automated notice if usage exceeds scheduled allotment by >20% in a rolling 7-day window.

- Bridge credits: we can apply the $75k as usage credits that count towards the first quarter of committed spend. The credits will also be eligible for true-up calculations (so they effectively reduce net committed spend required).

I'll drop an updated pricing tab into the workbook and can host a 30-minute session Tue 10:30am PDT to walk through. Naomi, can you confirm call?

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Alicia / team — following our call this morning, summary and agreed next steps below. Thanks to everyone for moving quickly.

Agreed commercial outline (as discussed and captured in updated workbook):
- 12-month renewal term, effective 2027-04-01.
- 6-month anchored rate: current effective per-token rate preserved for months 1-6 provided the 40% minimum commit is met with a 90-day ramp and a 30-day review checkpoint.
- Consumption-tier swap: months 7-12 transition to the blended 3-tier schedule included in the pricing workbook.
- Bridge credits: $75,000 applied as invoice credits to be consumed against usage in Q1 of the renewal; will show as a line-item credit on invoices.
- Dedicated burst pool: guaranteed access to 6 A100-equivalent cards during four scheduled 2-hour windows per day; out-of-window access at 1.4x anchor rate. No separate fixed reservation fee.

1) Naomi to update SOW and pricing workbook (attached).
